references.name: The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money
references.connection: The intellectual framework behind government spending and fiscal policy as alternatives to monetary policy

references.name: John Maynard Keynes, Auri Sacra Fames
references.desc: Essay on gold's retreat from circulation
references.connection: Quoted extensively on gold's disappearance from everyday use and the rationalizing that follows

references.name: Milton Friedman & Anna Schwartz, A Monetary History of the United States, 1867–1960
references.connection: Bernstein admits ignoring this in the original; Friedman's dictum that "inflation is always and everywhere a monetary phenomenon" proved more right than Bernstein's view

references.name: Robert Heilbroner & Peter Bernstein, A Primer on Government Spending
references.desc: Co-authored 1963 polemic for Kennedy tax cut
references.connection: The book that spawned this one; sold 100,000+ copies with a full-page NYT ad by Bennett Cerf

references.name: Walter Bagehot, Lombard Street
references.connection: Source of "John Bull cannot stand two percent" — the minimum return required to justify lending

references.name: D.H. Robertson, Money
references.connection: Recommended further reading; cited for its freshness and insights despite age

references.name: James Tobin, Stabilization Policy Ten Years After
references.connection: Cited in 2008 introduction as an example of how even top economists were slow to accept the primacy of money in controlling inflation

references.name: Robert V. Roosa, The Dollar and World Liquidity
references.desc: US Treasury official, international monetary policy
references.connection: Authoritative account of the transformation of US policy from "hard" gold to "paper" gold and Special Drawing Rights

references.name: Robert Triffin, Our International Monetary System
references.connection: Argues powerfully for rational new approaches to international reserves beyond gold and the dollar

references.name: A.J. Brown, The Great Inflation
references.connection: Cited for evidence that savings patterns don't break down until prices double in six months or less

references.name: Lawrence Ritter (ed.), Money and Economic Activity
references.connection: Covers the Gurley-Shaw thesis that non-bank financial institutions have effectively monetized savings, limiting the Fed's control

references.name: Jordi Gali & Mark Gertler, Journal of Economic Perspectives
references.connection: Cited in 2008 intro: "the policy process is as much, if not more, about communicating the future intentions of policy in a transparent way, as it is about choosing the current policy instrument"

references.name: Paul Volcker
references.connection: Wrote the 2008 foreword; his painful anti-inflation campaign is the definitive refutation of Bernstein's 1968 complacency about inflation
